issue_context.title: apt_repository for ppa's fails without apt-key executable, generates invalid source for current Debian Testing
issue_context.body:
### Summary

As noted in #84478, apt-key is going away, and the change to implement this was recently deployed to Debian Testing and from there will eventually bubble into all Debian and Debian-based distributions.

This change revealed that the code in apt_repository.py to add PPA repositories when apt-key doesn't exist, is broken. In particular, it tries to use `gpg --export` to receive a key from the Ubuntu key server, when in fact `--export` is for exporting from a keyring, not a key server. It really needs to do `gpg --recv-key` to fetch the key from the key server, followed by `gpg --export` to export it from the keyring it was received into, into a separate key file for use by apt.

However, this by itself is not sufficient, because the other change being made in Debian Testing is requiring sources to be explicitly bound to specific keys, i.e., `signed-by` needs to be specified. Therefore, in addition to fixing the incorrect usage of `gpg`, we also need to fix the PPA code so that it inserts a `signed-by` assignment into the source line.

The attached patch makes fixes both of these issues, including attempting to account, imperfectly, for the fact that the signed-by setting may or may not be in the source entry when a task attempts to remove a PPA.

I do _not_ have time to write tests for this. I do _not_ have time to put together a PR and nurse it through the process of getting it merged. Do with this patch what you will.

[apt_repository_patch.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18387424/apt_repository_patch.txt)
